body:
## Problem

The `{ breaking: true, type: "chore", scope: "deps", release: "major" }` rule
assumes `chore(deps)!` means "a breaking npm dependency change". In this repo
Renovate also emits `chore(deps)!` for GitHub Actions and pre-commit hook
updates, which change nothing in the published package.

The `{ type: "chore", scope: "actions", release: false }` rule does not protect
these, because Renovate did not use the `actions` scope for them.

## Evidence

All 11 `chore(deps)!` commits in history, checked against the `files` allowlist
in package.json (`index.cjs`, `wrapper.mjs`, `scripts/*`):

| Commit | Subject | Touches a published file |
| --- | --- | --- |
| b295667 | update actions/setup-node (v6.4.0 - v7.0.0) | NONE |
| 43fddc6 | update actions/cache (v5.0.5 - v6.0.0) | NONE |
| c229f94 | update actions/checkout (v6.0.3 - v7.0.0) | NONE |
| 7e0a040 | update ivuorinen/actions | NONE |
| e74985b | update actions/cache (v4.3.0 - v5.0.0) | NONE |
| 405a68d | update renovatebot/pre-commit-hooks | NONE |
| bcfea58 | update github/codeql-action (v3 - v4) | NONE |
| fa87391 | update conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits | package.json |
| d27f564 | update undici (7.24.6 - 8.0.2) | package.json |
| c068314 | update @ivuorinen/config-checker | package.json |
| 8936758 | update semantic-release (24.2.3 - 25.0.0) | package.json |

7 of 11 (64%) touch no published file. Scope counts over the last 60 commits:
`chore(deps)` 27, `chore(actions)` 12, `chore(deps)!` 5 - so the `actions`
scope is used for some action updates but not all.

`.github/renovate.json` in this repo contains no `semanticCommitScope` pin; it
only extends `github>ivuorinen/renovate-config`.

## Impact

This repo consumes its own config (`.releaserc.json` extends `./index.cjs`).
After this change, the next `chore(deps)!: update actions/checkout`-style
commit publishes a **major** version of `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config`
whose tarball is byte-identical to the previous release. On the historical
rate that is roughly 7 spurious majors. Every consuming repo pinned to `^1`
stops receiving updates until someone bumps the range by hand.

The change is still correct for its stated purpose - a breaking npm dependency
must not reach `^1.x` consumers silently. The defect is that the trigger is
broader than the intent.

## Fix

Make Renovate's scope match the intent, in `github>ivuorinen/renovate-config`
(or override locally in `.github/renovate.json`), so that action and
pre-commit managers emit `chore(actions)` rather than `chore(deps)`:

```json
{
  "packageRules": [
    {
      "matchManagers": ["github-actions", "pre-commit"],
      "semanticCommitScope": "actions"
    }
  ]
}
```

With that in place `chore(actions)!` stays at `release: false` (verified in
test/release-rules.test.mjs) and only genuine npm dependency breaks reach the
major rule.

Until the Renovate side lands, expect majors from CI-only bumps. Do not fix
this by widening the `actions` rule or by reverting the `deps` rule to minor -
both re-open the original defect.
EOF # ctx-ok

## Resolution
Added a local packageRules override in .github/renovate.json pinning semanticCommitScope=actions for the github-actions and pre-commit managers, so CI-only bumps land as chore(actions) and stay at release:false. Residual: only this repo is covered. Other repos consuming @ivuorinen/semantic-release-config via github>ivuorinen/renovate-config still emit chore(deps)! for action bumps and will cut spurious majors until the same rule lands in the shared preset. Unverifiable until Renovate next opens a PR here.
title: chore(deps)! is used for CI-only updates, so the new major rule will cut majors for changes that do not ship

## Problem

`.mega-linter.yml` is committed, configured in detail (ENABLE_LINTERS, SARIF
reporting, a zizmor `GITHUB_TOKEN` workaround), and enables `JAVASCRIPT_ES` and
`TYPESCRIPT_ES` pointed at a config file that does not exist. No workflow in the
repo runs MegaLinter.

## Evidence

```
.mega-linter.yml:36: JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
.mega-linter.yml:37: TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
```

```
$ git ls-files | grep eslint
eslint.config.mjs
```

There is no `.eslintrc.json`; the repo uses ESLint flat config
(`eslint.config.mjs`), which MegaLinter would not read from that variable.

No workflow references MegaLinter:

```
$ git ls-files .github/workflows
codeql.yml  pr-lint.yml  publish.yml  stale.yml  sync-labels.yml
```

None of these mention `megalinter` or `mega-linter`.

## Impact

If `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint` is MegaLinter under the hood, the JS/TS linters
run against a missing config -- they either fall back to defaults or skip
silently, and either way the flat config in this repo is not what is enforced.
If `pr-lint` is not MegaLinter, the entire file is dead configuration that
future maintainers will read as active policy.

## Fix

Determine which is true, then:

- MegaLinter is used -> drop the two stale lines (MegaLinter's `JAVASCRIPT_ES`
  descriptor autodetects `eslint.config.mjs`):

  ```yaml
  # remove:
  JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
  TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
  ```

  Also drop `TYPESCRIPT_ES` -- there is no TypeScript in the repo.

- MegaLinter is not used -> `git rm .mega-linter.yml`.

Do not leave it as-is; a config file that names a path that does not exist is
worse than no config file.

## Resolution
Premise disproven. ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint IS MegaLinter (oxsecurity/megalinter/flavors/cupcake@v9.6.0, action.yml:662-665), invoked by both pr-lint.yml and publish.yml, so .mega-linter.yml is wired, not dead. The stale JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE path is real but belongs in a finding with the correct premise. Refiled as audit-1f0e37fe.
title: MegaLinter config points at a nonexistent .eslintrc.json and no workflow invokes MegaLinter

body:
## Problem

`package.json` defines `"test": "node --test \"test/**/*.test.mjs\""` and
`test/release-rules.test.mjs` asserts the exact release each commit pattern must
produce. No workflow ever runs it. The suite is decorative.

## Evidence

Every `run:` step across all five workflows:

```
$ grep -rn "yarn test\|npm test\|node --test\|run: " .github/workflows/
.github/workflows/publish.yml:61:  run: npm install -g corepack --force && corepack enable
.github/workflows/publish.yml:73:  run: yarn install
```

`publish.yml` is `Linter` (a `pr-lint` composite action) -> `publish`. There is
no test job and no `needs:` on one. `pr-lint.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `stale.yml`,
and `sync-labels.yml` contain no test step either.

The `pr-lint` action does not run tests either. It is MegaLinter
(`oxsecurity/megalinter/flavors/cupcake@v9.6.0`, `pr-lint/action.yml:662-665`).
It detects `package.json`, sets up Node 24, and runs `yarn install --immutable`
-- so the dependencies are installed and `yarn test` would work -- then goes
straight to linting:

```
$ grep -n "yarn test\|npm test\|node --test\|bun test\|phpunit" pr-lint/action.yml
(no output — 724 lines, no test invocation)
```

So the only gate in front of `npm publish` is a linter.

Locally the suite passes and is meaningful:

```
$ node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"
# tests 7  pass 7  fail 0
```

The file's own header states what it guards: "dropping the breaking chore(deps)
rule silently downgrades it to patch, and a global `{ breaking: true }` rule
would make chore(actions)! cut a major."

## Impact

Both named regressions ship to npm without a gate. An edit to `index.cjs` that
drops `{ breaking: true, type: "chore", scope: "deps", release: "major" }` turns
every breaking dependency update into a patch that reaches `^1.x` consumers
silently -- the exact failure the rule exists to prevent -- and `main` publishes
it. Every consuming repo inherits the broken rule set.

## Fix

Add a gating test job to `publish.yml` and make `publish` depend on it:

```yaml
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
      - run: npm install -g corepack --force && corepack enable
      - run: yarn install --immutable
      - run: yarn test

  publish:
    needs:
      - Linter
      - test
```

Mirror the same job into `pr-lint.yml` so pull requests fail before merge, not
after publish.

## Resolution
Added a gating 'test' job to publish.yml (publish now needs: [Linter, test]) and to pr-lint.yml so PRs fail before merge. Both check out, use node-version-file .nvmrc, corepack, 'yarn install --immutable', 'yarn test'. Verified: 7 tests pass, actionlint clean on both workflows.
title: The test suite never runs in CI, so the release-rule regressions it guards can publish unblocked

body:
## Problem

`eslint.config.mjs:1` does `import ivuorinenConfig from "@ivuorinen/eslint-config";`.
That package appears nowhere in `package.json` -- neither `dependencies` nor
`devDependencies` -- and is not installed. `eslint` itself is also not a
declared or installed dependency.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -n "eslint" package.json
(no output)

$ node -e "require.resolve('@ivuorinen/eslint-config')"
NOT INSTALLED: MODULE_NOT_FOUND

$ ls node_modules/.bin/ | grep -i eslint
(no output)

$ ls node_modules/@ivuorinen/
config-checker
```

`index.cjs` and `scripts/postinstall.cjs` carry per-file `/* eslint ... */`
directives (postinstall.cjs:3), so the code is written as though ESLint runs.
It never has in a clean checkout.

This also breaks in CI, not just locally. `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint` is
MegaLinter (`oxsecurity/megalinter/flavors/cupcake@v9.6.0`), it runs
`yarn install --immutable` before linting (`pr-lint/action.yml:176-201`), and
`.mega-linter.yml:30` enables `JAVASCRIPT_ES`. The cupcake image ships eslint
10.8.0 and a fixed plugin set, not `@ivuorinen/eslint-config`, and `yarn install`
cannot supply it either because it is not in `package.json`. So the CI ESLint
run cannot resolve `eslint.config.mjs` either.

It has not surfaced yet because the action pins `VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE: false`
(`pr-lint/action.yml:684`), so only files in the diff are linted -- and exactly
one of the last 40 commits touched a `.cjs`/`.mjs` file. The failure is latent,
not absent: the next PR that edits `index.cjs` triggers it.

## Impact

The two `eslint-disable` comments and the whole flat config are unenforced. Any
contributor who runs `npx eslint .` gets a resolution failure, not a lint
result. The first PR to touch a JS file gets a CI failure inside a container
image, with a resolution error naming a package that is not in `package.json`.

## Fix

Either wire it or delete it. To wire it:

```sh
yarn add --dev eslint @ivuorinen/eslint-config
```

and add a script plus a CI step:

```json
"scripts": {
  "lint": "eslint .",
  "test": "node --test \"test/**/*.test.mjs\""
}
```

Deleting `eslint.config.mjs` instead is not a valid alternative here: `pr-lint`
is MegaLinter and MegaLinter reads the repository's own ESLint config, so
removing it would silently fall back to the image's default rules rather than
delegating to a configured linter.

## Resolution
Added eslint@^10 and @ivuorinen/eslint-config@^1.5.6 as devDependencies plus a 'lint' script. First run immediately produced the 2 real errors the finding predicted were latent (object-shorthand and no-restricted-properties on assert.equal in test/release-rules.test.mjs); both fixed (logger: { log() {} }, assert.strictEqual). 'yarn lint' now exits 0 and the 7 tests still pass.
title: eslint.config.mjs imports an undeclared, uninstalled package, so ESLint cannot run in this repo

body:
## Problem

`ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint` is MegaLinter, so `.mega-linter.yml` is live
configuration -- but four of its settings have no effect, and one of those
silently removes workflow security scanning from CI.

## Evidence

`pr-lint/action.yml:662-665` in `ivuorinen/actions`:

```yaml
    - name: MegaLinter
      uses: oxsecurity/megalinter/flavors/cupcake@ef3e84b8b836d76db562d0f3ed7da61e8fd538bc # v9.6.0
      id: ml
```

**1. `VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE` and `APPLY_FIXES` are overridden.** The action sets
both in the step's `env:` block (`action.yml:684, 689`), and MegaLinter resolves
environment variables ahead of `.mega-linter.yml`:

| `.mega-linter.yml` | `pr-lint/action.yml` env | Effective |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `APPLY_FIXES: all` (:13) | `APPLY_FIXES: none` (:689) | `none` |
| `VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE: true` (:16) | `VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE: false` (:684) | `false` |

**2. `JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE` names a file that does not exist.**

```
.mega-linter.yml:36: JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json
.mega-linter.yml:37: TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE: .eslintrc.json

$ git ls-files | grep eslint
eslint.config.mjs
```

`TYPESCRIPT_ES` is enabled with no TypeScript file in the repository.

**3. `ENABLE_LINTERS` is an allowlist, so `ACTION_ZIZMOR` never runs.**

```yaml
ENABLE_LINTERS:
  - YAML_YAMLLINT
  - MARKDOWN_MARKDOWNLINT
  - JAVASCRIPT_ES
  - TYPESCRIPT_ES
```

`ACTION_ZIZMOR` is not listed, so the eight-line
`ACTION_ZIZMOR_UNSECURED_ENV_VARIABLES` workaround at the top of the file
(`.mega-linter.yml:6-11`) configures a linter that is disabled, and
`.github/zizmor.yml` is read by nothing. `DISABLE_LINTERS: [REPOSITORY_DEVSKIM]`
is redundant for the same reason -- an allowlist already excludes it.

Nor does anything else run zizmor or actionlint in CI:

```
$ grep -rn "zizmor\|actionlint\|pre-commit" .github/workflows/
(no output)
```

`FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE` (`.mega-linter.yml:39-40`) additionally excludes
`.github/workflows`, so workflow files would be skipped even if the linters were
enabled. actionlint runs only in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, on developer
machines.

## Impact

The npm-publishing workflow in this repo -- the one holding `NPM_TOKEN` and a
`PAT` -- is scanned by zizmor only when a contributor happens to have pre-commit
installed locally. `.github/zizmor.yml` reads as active suppression policy while
suppressing nothing.

`VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE: false` also means JS linting only runs when a JS file is
in the diff. Of the last 40 commits exactly one touched `index.cjs`, which is
why the broken ESLint setup in `audit-8cc51c37` has not surfaced yet.

## Fix

In `.mega-linter.yml`: drop the two overridden settings, fix the ESLint config
reference, and add the security linters to the allowlist.

```yaml
ENABLE_LINTERS:
  - ACTION_ACTIONLINT
  - ACTION_ZIZMOR
  - JAVASCRIPT_ES
  - MARKDOWN_MARKDOWNLINT
  - YAML_YAMLLINT
```

- delete `APPLY_FIXES: all` and `VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE: true` (the action wins;
  keeping them documents a behaviour the repo does not have)
- delete `JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE` and `TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE` -- the
  `JAVASCRIPT_ES` descriptor autodetects `eslint.config.mjs`
- delete `TYPESCRIPT_ES` and `DISABLE_LINTERS`
- drop `\.github/workflows` from `FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE` so the newly enabled
  workflow linters have files to read

## Resolution
Rewrote .mega-linter.yml: removed APPLY_FIXES and VALIDATE_ALL_CODEBASE (overridden by the action's step env), removed JAVASCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE/TYPESCRIPT_ES_CONFIG_FILE and TYPESCRIPT_ES, removed the redundant DISABLE_LINTERS, added ACTION_ACTIONLINT and ACTION_ZIZMOR to ENABLE_LINTERS, and dropped .github/workflows from FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE so the workflow linters have files to read. Enabling zizmor surfaced a real adhoc-packages finding on the corepack step in the new pr-lint.yml test job; added pr-lint.yml to the existing ignore list in .github/zizmor.yml alongside publish.yml. zizmor now reports 'No findings to report'.
title: Four of .mega-linter.yml's settings are dead: two are overridden by the action, one names a missing file, and the ENABLE_LINTERS allowlist silently disables zizmor

## Problem

`publish.yml:15-16` sets the npm publish token at workflow scope:

```yaml
env:
  NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

Workflow-level `env` applies to every job. The `Linter` job needs no npm
credential, yet runs with the publish token in its process environment.

## Evidence

The `Linter` job (`publish.yml:19-31`) has one step:

```yaml
      - name: Run PR Lint
        uses: ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint@94a4f68a6b95ecc1677fbcac1683119fd869adf7
```

That composite action, and every tool it shells out to, inherits `NPM_TOKEN`.

The workflow-level definition is also redundant: the only step that consumes the
token sets it itself at step scope (`publish.yml:75-79`):

```yaml
      - name: Semantic Release
        uses: cycjimmy/semantic-release-action@b12c8f6015dc215fe37bc154d4ad456dd3833c90
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

Removing lines 15-16 changes nothing about what the publish step receives.

## Impact

A publish-capable npm token for the `@ivuorinen` scope reaches a linting job
that has no reason to hold it. Any compromise of the pinned `pr-lint` action
ref, or of any linter it invokes, exfiltrates a token that can publish arbitrary
code as `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` -- a package whose `postinstall`
runs on every consumer install. The blast radius is every downstream repo.

## Fix

Delete the workflow-level block; the step-level env already covers the real use:

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions: {}

jobs:
  Linter:
```

(remove `publish.yml:15-16` entirely.)

## Resolution
Deleted the workflow-level 'env: NPM_TOKEN' block from publish.yml. The Semantic Release step already sets NPM_TOKEN at step scope, so the publish path is unchanged and the Lint and Test jobs no longer see the token.
title: NPM_TOKEN is set workflow-wide, exposing the publish token to the Lint job that does not need it

body:
## Problem

`package.json:46-51` declares as runtime `dependencies`:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@ivuorinen/config-checker": "^2.2.17",
  "@semantic-release/github": "^12.0.8",
  "conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits": "^10.0.0",
  "semantic-release": "^25.0.5"
}
```

`index.cjs` references plugins only by name string. semantic-release resolves
those from its own dependency tree, so `@semantic-release/github` here is
redundant, and `semantic-release` itself is the consumer's tool, not this
package's runtime requirement.

## Evidence

semantic-release already ships all four plugins named in `index.cjs`:

```
$ node -e "const p=require('./node_modules/semantic-release/package.json'); \
  console.log(Object.keys(p.dependencies).filter(k=>k.startsWith('@semantic-release')))"
@semantic-release/commit-analyzer@^13.0.1
@semantic-release/error@^4.0.0
@semantic-release/github@^12.0.0
@semantic-release/npm@^13.1.1
@semantic-release/release-notes-generator@^14.1.0
```

`@semantic-release/npm` and `@semantic-release/release-notes-generator` are also
named in `index.cjs` and are *not* declared here -- proving the string-name
plugins resolve fine without a direct declaration. `@semantic-release/github` is
declared inconsistently with its two siblings.

Cost of the current declaration, measured on a clean consumer:

```
$ npm pack --dry-run          # the package itself
unpackedSize 10296            # 6 files, ~10 KB

$ npm install ./ivuorinen-semantic-release-config-1.1.23.tgz
added 301 packages in 9s
```

`conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits` is a genuine direct dependency (the
`conventionalcommits` preset silently falls back to `angular` without it) and
must stay.

## Impact

A consumer that pins its own `semantic-release` to a different major gets two
copies in the tree; the CLI it invokes and the version this config drags in
diverge, and `extends` resolution can land on either. Consumers who deliberately
avoid `@semantic-release/github` (GitLab, Gitea, npm-only releases) still
install it and its octokit tree.

## Fix

Move the tool to `peerDependencies` and drop the redundant plugin:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@ivuorinen/config-checker": "^2.2.17",
  "conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits": "^10.0.0"
},
"peerDependencies": {
  "semantic-release": ">=24"
},
"devDependencies": {
  "@semantic-release/commit-analyzer": "^13.0.1",
  "semantic-release": "^25.0.5"
}
```

This is a breaking change for consumers who relied on the transitive install --
release it as `chore(deps)!:` or `feat!:` so it cuts a major, which is exactly
what `index.cjs` already encodes.

## Resolution
Moved semantic-release to peerDependencies (>=24) plus devDependencies, and dropped the redundant @semantic-release/github. CORRECTION to the finding's Impact: the '301 packages' figure does not improve for a bare consumer, because npm 7+ auto-installs peerDependencies -- re-measured at 301 either way. The real, measured win is the case the finding was actually about: a consumer that already has semantic-release now adds 4 packages instead of a second nested copy. Verified @semantic-release/github still resolves from semantic-release's own tree and the postinstall still writes .releaserc.json.
title: semantic-release and @semantic-release/github are runtime dependencies of a config package, forcing 301 packages on consumers

body:
## Problem

`scripts/postinstall.cjs:10` calls `checkConfig("release")` with no path
argument. `@ivuorinen/config-checker` reads `process.env.INIT_CWD` with no
fallback and passes it straight to `path.join`, so an unset `INIT_CWD` throws
before any try/catch.

Line 19 of the same file already guards the same variable:

```js
const filePath = path.join(process.env.INIT_CWD || process.cwd(), ".releaserc.json");
```

The guard exists at line 19; the crash happens at line 10. That inconsistency is
the defect -- the author anticipated the unset case and protected only the later
of the two uses.

## Evidence

`node_modules/@ivuorinen/config-checker/lib/config-checker.js:16,29`:

```js
let searchPath = process.env.INIT_CWD;
...
return allFiles.filter((file) => fs.existsSync(path.join(searchPath, file)));
```

Reproduced:

```
$ env -u INIT_CWD node scripts/postinstall.cjs
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "path" argument must be of type string. Received undefined
    at Object.join (node:path:1339:7)
    at .../config-checker/lib/config-checker.js:29:55
EXIT=1
```

With the variable set it works and is idempotent:

```
$ INIT_CWD=$tmp node scripts/postinstall.cjs
exit=0   # writes $tmp/.releaserc.json
```

`npm install` and `bun install` of the packed tarball both set `INIT_CWD` and
both succeed, so the crash is not reachable through those two package managers
today. It is reachable by running the script directly (which `CONTRIBUTING.md`
does not forbid), by any runner or container step that invokes it outside a
package manager, and by any manager that does not set `INIT_CWD`.

## Impact

Where reachable, a non-zero postinstall aborts the whole install. The failure
mode is a stack trace naming a third-party file, not this package, so the
consumer has no obvious path to the cause. The convenience feature the script
provides is not worth failing an install for.

## Fix

`config-checker` already accepts an explicit search path as its second argument
(`configChecker(moduleName, pathPrefix = "")`). Use the same fallback line 19
uses, and hoist it to one constant:

```js
const cwd = process.env.INIT_CWD || process.cwd();
const foundConfig = checkConfig("release", cwd);
...
const filePath = path.join(cwd, ".releaserc.json");
```

## Resolution
Hoisted 'const cwd = process.env.INIT_CWD || process.cwd()' and passed it to checkConfig('release', cwd) via config-checker's existing pathPrefix argument; the write at the bottom reuses the same constant. Verified: 'env -u INIT_CWD node scripts/postinstall.cjs' now exits 0 and writes .releaserc.json where it previously threw ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE and exited 1.
title: postinstall crashes with an uncaught TypeError when INIT_CWD is unset, ten lines before its own INIT_CWD fallback

body:
## Problem

`CLAUDE.md` under `## Verification`:

```md
No test suite — verify config loads and inspect the output.
```

There is a test suite. `test/release-rules.test.mjs` exists, `package.json:44`
defines `"test": "node --test \"test/**/*.test.mjs\""`, and it passes.

## Evidence

```
$ node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"
# tests 7  pass 7  fail 0
```

`CLAUDE.md` `## Key Files` lists `index.cjs`, `wrapper.mjs`,
`scripts/postinstall.cjs`, `.releaserc.json` -- and omits `test/`.

`CONTRIBUTING.md:55-59` has the same gap: "Verify the config loads correctly"
followed only by the `node -e "console.log(...)"` one-liner, never `yarn test`.

## Impact

`CLAUDE.md` is loaded into every agent session in this repo as authoritative
project instruction. It tells the agent, in so many words, that running tests is
not possible here. An agent editing `index.cjs` follows it, verifies with the
load check -- which passes for any syntactically valid object, including one
with the `breaking: true` chore(deps) rule deleted -- and reports success. That
is the same regression finding `audit-c9272141` describes, reached from the
documentation side.

## Fix

`CLAUDE.md`:

```md

```sh
yarn test        # node --test over test/*.test.mjs — asserts each commit
                 # pattern produces the expected release
```
```

and add `test/release-rules.test.mjs — asserts the release rules in index.cjs`
to `## Key Files`.

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, replacing step 3 of the Development Workflow:

```md
3. Run the tests:

   ```sh
   yarn test
   ```
```

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md: replaced 'No test suite' with a 'yarn test' Verification block that states why the config-load check is not a substitute, and added test/release-rules.test.mjs to Key Files. CONTRIBUTING.md: 'yarn test' is now step 3 of the Development Workflow, with the load check demoted to optional step 4.
title: CLAUDE.md states there is no test suite, instructing every agent to skip the seven tests that guard the release rules

## Problem

`publish.yml:42` grants an OIDC token to the publish job:

```yaml
      id-token: write # to enable use of OIDC for npm provenance
```

Nothing in the repo enables provenance, so the permission is granted and unused.

## Evidence

Provenance requires either `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE=true` in the publish step's
environment or `"provenance": true` under `publishConfig`. Neither exists:

```
$ grep -rn "provenance" package.json .github/
.github/workflows/publish.yml:42:      id-token: write # to enable use of OIDC for npm provenance
.github/zizmor.yml:8:  use-trusted-publishing:
```

`package.json:35-37`:

```json
"publishConfig": {
  "access": "public"
}
```

`.github/zizmor.yml:8-10` suppresses the scanner rule that would flag this:

```yaml
  use-trusted-publishing:
    # npm trusted publishing requires registry-side setup; tracked separately
    ignore:
      - publish.yml
```

## Impact

Published tarballs carry no provenance attestation, so consumers cannot verify
which workflow built them -- the security property the comment claims. Meanwhile
the job holds an OIDC token that any compromised step could exchange for a
cloud identity. Granted-but-unused privilege is the worst of both.

## Fix

Enable what the permission is for:

```yaml
      - name: Semantic Release
        uses: cycjimmy/semantic-release-action@b12c8f6015dc215fe37bc154d4ad456dd3833c90 # v6.0.0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: true
```

If provenance is deliberately deferred until npm trusted publishing is set up
(as `.github/zizmor.yml` states), drop `id-token: write` until then and restore
it in the same commit that enables provenance.

## Resolution
Added NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: true to the Semantic Release step env in publish.yml, making the existing id-token: write permission meaningful. Note: this is the first release that will attempt provenance; if the registry rejects it the publish fails, and the documented alternative is to drop id-token: write instead.
title: publish.yml grants id-token: write for npm provenance that is never enabled

## Problem

`README.md:70-109` gives consumers a copy-paste release workflow. It contradicts
the hardening this repo applies to its own workflows on three points.

## Evidence

README example vs `.github/workflows/publish.yml`:

| README | This repo's publish.yml |
| --- | --- |
| `actions/checkout@v4` (README:90) | `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1` (:46) |
| `actions/setup-node@v4` (README:95) | `actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0` (:52) |
| no `persist-credentials: false` | `persist-credentials: false` (:48) |
| no top-level `permissions: {}` | `permissions: {}` (:13) |

The repo runs zizmor (`.github/zizmor.yml`) and pins every action to a full
commit SHA, so the unpinned-tag pattern is one it has deliberately rejected for
itself.

The example also grants `id-token: write` (README:86) while running plain
`npx semantic-release` with no provenance flag, so the permission does nothing --
see `audit-a9bb9c69` on the same defect in `publish.yml`.

## Impact

A mutable `@v4` tag can be repointed by anyone who compromises the action
repository; the consumer's workflow then runs attacker code with
`contents: write` and an `NPM_TOKEN` in scope. Leaving the checkout token
persisted in `.git/config` widens that further. This README is the setup
instruction for every downstream repo, so the weak pattern propagates.

## Fix

Bring the example in line with `publish.yml`:

```yaml
permissions: {}

jobs:
  release:
    name: Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          always-auth: true
          node-version: 20
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
      - run: npm ci
      - name: Release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: npx semantic-release
```

`id-token: write` is dropped because the example does not enable provenance; add
it back together with `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: true` if the example should teach
provenance.

## Resolution
README workflow example now pins actions/checkout and actions/setup-node to the same commit SHAs publish.yml uses, adds persist-credentials: false and a top-level 'permissions: {}', comments each job permission, and adds NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: true so id-token: write is not granted for nothing. Added a short paragraph explaining the SHA pinning and how to opt out of provenance.
title: The README workflow example teaches unpinned action tags and credential persistence that the repo's own workflows reject

## Problem

`.gitignore:70`:

```
!*.svg  # comment out if you don't need vector files
```

Git supports `#` only at the start of a line. A `#` after a pattern is literal
text, so the pattern is the whole 48-character string, which matches no file.

## Evidence

```
$ printf 'a.svg\n' > /tmp/g/.gitignore-test
$ cat .gitignore | sed -n '69,71p'
[._]*.s[a-v][a-z]
!*.svg  # comment out if you don't need vector files
[._]*.sw[a-p]
```

Line 69 `[._]*.s[a-v][a-z]` matches `.a.svg`-style vim swap names; line 70 is
meant to re-include `.svg` files from it. It cannot, because Git looks for a
file literally named `*.svg  # comment out if you don't need vector files`.

The repo currently tracks no `.svg` files, so the effect is latent, not active.

## Impact

The negation silently does nothing. If an SVG asset is ever added under a name
line 69 matches, it is ignored and the author gets no signal -- a
disappearing-file bug that takes a `git check-ignore -v` run to diagnose.

## Fix

Put the comment on its own line:

```
# comment out the next line if you don't need vector files
!*.svg
```

## Resolution
The offending line is gone: .gitignore was rewritten (see audit-6b340e27) and no longer contains the vim-swap patterns the !*.svg negation existed to escape, so neither the negation nor its trailing comment remain.
title: A trailing comment in .gitignore is parsed as part of the pattern, so the !*.svg negation never applies

## Problem

The repository publishes six files and carries three ignore/lint configs that
cover nothing in it.

## Evidence

`.yamlignore` is zero bytes:

```
$ wc -c .yamlignore
0 .yamlignore
```

The plausible reason to keep it -- that yamllint crashes without it -- was
tested and does not hold. yamllint 1.38.0 produces byte-identical output and
exit 0 with the file present and absent, and the pre-commit hook passes either
way:

```
$ yamllint -c .yamllint.yml .            # with .yamlignore
EXIT=0
$ mv .yamlignore /tmp && yamllint -c .yamllint.yml .   # without
EXIT=0                                   # identical output
$ pre-commit run yamllint --all-files
yamllint.................................................................Passed
```

yamllint has no `.yamlignore` concept at all -- its mechanisms are the `ignore:`
and `ignore-from-file:` keys inside `.yamllint.yml`, neither of which this
repo's `.yamllint.yml` uses:

```
$ grep -rn "yamlignore" <yamllint-1.38.0-install>/
(no occurrences)
```

MegaLinter does not read it either (`ACTION`/`YAML` descriptors use
`*_FILTER_REGEX_EXCLUDE` and `.megalinterignore`); a code search across
`oxsecurity/megalinter` for `yamlignore` returns 0 results.

`.shellcheckrc` disables a rule for shell scripts that do not exist:

```
$ cat .shellcheckrc
disable=SC2129

$ git ls-files | grep -E '\.(sh|bash)$'
(no output)
```

`.pre-commit-config.yaml:34` runs actionlint with `-shellcheck=` -- shellcheck
explicitly disabled -- so even the `run:` blocks inside workflows are not
shellchecked.

`.gitignore` is 135 lines covering PHP CS Fixer, Composer, PHPUnit, Laravel
(`bootstrap/compiled.php`, `app/storage/`, `Homestead.yaml`), Vagrant, Next.js,
Nuxt, Vercel, Docusaurus, Gatsby, Parcel, Bower, Grunt, JetBrains, Vim, and
Crashlytics. The repo is `index.cjs`, `wrapper.mjs`, `scripts/postinstall.cjs`,
one test, and config. `/node_modules` and `node_modules/` are both listed
(lines 30 and 123); `out` and `out/` (52, 100); `/coverage` and `coverage`
(126, 23).

## Impact

Nothing breaks. The cost is that a reader cannot tell which of these files is
policy and which is copy-paste residue, so none of them get maintained -- and
`.mega-linter.yml` (see `audit-577679ae`) is the case where that residue turned
into a live config naming a file that does not exist.

`.github/zizmor.yml` belongs on the same list for a different reason: it is not
residue, but `ENABLE_LINTERS` in `.mega-linter.yml` is an allowlist that omits
`ACTION_ZIZMOR`, and no workflow runs zizmor directly, so nothing reads it. That
is tracked in `audit-577679ae` because the fix is to enable the linter, not to
delete the config.

## Fix

```sh
git rm .yamlignore .shellcheckrc
```

and reduce `.gitignore` to what this repository can actually produce:

```
node_modules/
coverage/
*.log
*.tgz
.env*
.DS_Store
.yarn/*
!.yarn/patches
!.yarn/releases
!.yarn/plugins
!.yarn/versions
node-compile-cache
```

Restore `.shellcheckrc` if and when a shell script is added and `-shellcheck=`
is removed from the actionlint hook.

## Resolution
Removed .yamlignore (git rm) and cut .gitignore from 135 lines to 33 grouped, deduplicated lines covering only what this repo produces. DEVIATION from the filed fix: .shellcheckrc was deliberately KEPT rather than deleted, because the same run enabled ACTION_ACTIONLINT in .mega-linter.yml and stopped excluding .github/workflows -- actionlint shellchecks the 'run:' blocks in those workflows, so .shellcheckrc is now live config rather than dead. .github/zizmor.yml likewise stays and is now read, since ACTION_ZIZMOR is enabled.
title: Three lint and ignore configs are dead: .yamlignore is empty, .shellcheckrc guards no shell scripts, .gitignore is 135 lines of unrelated boilerplate

## Problem

`index.cjs:12` maps every `chore(deps)` to a patch release:

```js
{ type: "chore", scope: "deps", release: "patch" },
```

Almost all `chore(deps)` traffic in this repo is lockfile-only -- transitive
security bumps that never reach the published tarball. Each one still publishes
a new version to npm.

## Evidence

Published files are `index.cjs`, `wrapper.mjs`, `scripts/postinstall.cjs`,
`package.json`, `README.md`, `LICENSE.md`:

```
$ npm pack --dry-run
LICENSE.md  README.md  index.cjs  package.json  scripts/postinstall.cjs  wrapper.mjs
```

Across the last 40 commits, exactly one touched a runtime-published file:

```
83b07a3  index.cjs, README.md, package.json  feat!: release major for breaking dependency updates
```

The other 39 touched only `yarn.lock`, `.github/`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, or
`docs/`. Six of those additionally touched `package.json` -- all of them
`chore(deps): update yarn`, changing only the `packageManager` hash.

Scope distribution over the last 60 commits:

```
31 chore(deps)      <- patch release each
 9 chore(actions)   <- correctly no release
 5 chore(deps)!     <- major release each
```

The `chore(deps)` traffic is Dependabot ("bump X from A to B", "npm_and_yarn
group"), which is not covered by the `.github/renovate.json` scope override --
that rule only matches `matchManagers: ["github-actions", "pre-commit"]` and only
applies to Renovate.

## Impact

`@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` is at 1.1.23 with a version history mostly
made of releases whose runtime content is identical to the previous one. Every
consumer's dependency bot opens a PR for each; each PR costs a CI run and a
review. The release feed carries no signal about which versions actually changed
behavior.

## Fix

Route lockfile-only bumps to a non-releasing scope. Add a Dependabot config that
matches the Renovate override already in place:

```yaml
# .github/dependabot.yml
version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    commit-message:
      prefix: "chore(actions)"
```

This is defensible because none of these bumps reach consumers -- the tarball
carries no lockfile. Genuine direct-dependency changes still arrive via Renovate
as `chore(deps)` (or `chore(deps)!`) and keep cutting releases.

Do not instead widen `{ type: "chore", scope: "deps", release: false }` -- that
would also silence real dependency changes to
`conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits`, which do affect consumers.

## Resolution
Added .github/dependabot.yml pinning commit-message.prefix to 'chore(actions)' for the npm ecosystem, which index.cjs maps to release: false. Lockfile-only Dependabot bumps stop cutting no-op patch releases; Renovate-driven direct dependency changes still arrive as chore(deps) and still release. Comment in the file explains why this is safe (the tarball ships no lockfile).
title: Lockfile-only chore(deps) bumps cut patch releases of an unchanged package, 39 of the last 40 commits shipping nothing

## Problem

`package.json:29-34` declares a full dual entry surface with no `types`:

```json
"main": "index.cjs",
"module": "wrapper.mjs",
"exports": {
  "import": "./wrapper.mjs",
  "require": "./index.cjs"
}
```

There is no `types` field, no `typesVersions`, and no `.d.ts` in the packed
tarball.

## Evidence

```
$ npm pack --dry-run
LICENSE.md  README.md  index.cjs  package.json  scripts/postinstall.cjs  wrapper.mjs
```

`package.json:15-19` `files` lists `index.cjs`, `wrapper.mjs`, `scripts/*` -- a
declaration file would not ship even if one existed.

## Impact

A TypeScript consumer doing `import config from "@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config"`
in a `release.config.ts` gets TS7016 ("could not find a declaration file ...
implicitly has an 'any' type") under `noImplicitAny`, and has to write an
ambient module declaration or `@ts-ignore`. The common path -- a
`.releaserc.json` naming the package as a string -- is unaffected, which is why
this is Low.

## Fix

Ship a two-line declaration. Add `index.d.ts`:

```ts
import type { GlobalConfig } from "semantic-release";
declare const config: GlobalConfig;
export default config;
```

and wire it:

```json
"files": ["index.cjs", "index.d.ts", "wrapper.mjs", "scripts/*"],
"types": "index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  "types": "./index.d.ts",
  "import": "./wrapper.mjs",
  "require": "./index.cjs"
}
```

`types` must come first in the `exports` object -- conditions resolve in
declaration order.

If typed consumption is explicitly out of scope, say so in `README.md` instead;
the current state says nothing either way.

## Resolution
Added index.d.ts (GlobalConfig from semantic-release), a 'types' field, 'types' as the first condition in the exports map, and index.d.ts to the files allowlist. Verified npm pack now ships it: LICENSE.md README.md index.cjs index.d.ts package.json scripts/postinstall.cjs wrapper.mjs.

## Problem

The new `.github/dependabot.yml` labels every npm update `chore(actions)`, which `index.cjs` maps to `release: false`. Its header comment justifies this by asserting that Dependabot only ever touches `yarn.lock` here. The config does not make that true.

Dependabot's npm updater defaults to `versioning-strategy: increase`, which raises the minimum version requirement in `package.json` whenever a new version falls outside the declared range. `versioning-strategy: lockfile-only` is the option that produces the behaviour the comment describes, and it is not set.

The result: a bump to one of the three runtime `dependencies` — the ones that ship to consumers — is committed under a scope that cuts no release.

## Evidence

```yaml

# .github/dependabot.yml:4-18

# Dependabot only ever bumps yarn.lock here — the published tarball contains no

# lockfile (see `files` in package.json), so these updates change nothing for

# consumers. They must not cut a release, hence the `actions` scope, which

# index.cjs maps to `release: false`.

#

# Direct dependency changes still arrive via Renovate as chore(deps) and do cut

# releases.

version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    commit-message:
      prefix: "chore(actions)"
```

The rule the scope maps to:

```js
// index.cjs:13
{ type: "chore", scope: "actions", release: false },
```

The dependencies that would be caught, all of which are published in the tarball's `package.json`:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@ivuorinen/config-checker": "^2.2.17",
  "conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits": "^10.0.0",
  "semantic-release": "^25.0.5"
}
```

Every Dependabot commit in current history happens to be lockfile-only because each bump was an in-range transitive:

```
563f77a chore(deps): bump js-yaml ...        yarn.lock | 6 +++---
9fe4738 chore(deps): bump brace-expansion ... yarn.lock | 6 +++---
973817d chore(deps): bump ip-address ...      yarn.lock | 6 +++---
```

That is the sample that made the assumption look safe; it is not evidence that the manifest is out of scope. A `semantic-release` 25 → 26 bump falls outside `^25.0.5` and rewrites `package.json`.

`.github/dependabot.yml` is untracked — this is a proposed change, not shipped behaviour.

## Impact

Failure scenario: Dependabot opens `chore(actions): bump semantic-release from 25.0.5 to 26.0.0`, editing `package.json` and `yarn.lock`. It merges to `main`. `index.cjs:13` matches the `actions` scope and returns `release: false`, so no version is published. The manifest change sits unreleased on `main`.

The next releasing commit — say a `fix:` for something unrelated — publishes a **patch**. That patch tarball carries the new `semantic-release: ^26.0.0` range. Every consumer on `^1.x` picks it up on their next install and gets a major dependency swap delivered as a patch.

That is exactly the outcome `CLAUDE.md` states the release rules exist to prevent:

> `chore(deps)!:` → major (breaking dep update; consumers on `^1.x` must not get it silently)

The narrower, always-present version of the same defect: any manifest bump Dependabot makes is attributed to whichever unrelated commit next cuts a release, so the release notes never mention it. `conventional-changelog-conventionalcommits` is the sharpest case — `CLAUDE.md` lists it under Gotchas as the dependency whose absence makes the preset silently fall back to angular, and a major bump of it would ship unannounced.

## Fix

Make the config match its comment by restricting Dependabot to the lockfile:

```yaml
version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /
    versioning-strategy: lockfile-only
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    commit-message:
      prefix: "chore(actions)"
```

With `lockfile-only`, Dependabot never edits `package.json`, the header comment becomes accurate, and the `actions` scope is correct for everything it produces — manifest changes stay exclusively with Renovate, which uses `chore(deps)` / `chore(deps)!` and does cut releases.

Note that `lockfile-only` also suppresses Dependabot **security** updates that require a manifest change. Those are Renovate's job here (`619efde chore(deps): update dependency undici (8.5.0 → 8.9.0) [security]`), so the coverage gap is already filled; confirm `github>ivuorinen/renovate-config` enables `vulnerabilityAlerts` before relying on it.

## Resolution
Added `versioning-strategy: lockfile-only` to the npm update block, which makes the file's existing claim true — Dependabot can no longer rewrite dependency ranges in package.json, so everything it produces genuinely is lockfile-only and the chore(actions)/release:false scope is correct for all of it. Expanded the header comment to state that the option is load bearing, what the default `increase` strategy would have done, and that Renovate now owns manifest security updates since lockfile-only suppresses Dependabot's.
title: dependabot.yml assumes lockfile-only updates but does not configure them, so runtime dependency bumps get the no-release scope

## Problem

The `publish` job installs corepack from the npm registry with no version constraint, in the same job that later holds the npm publish token and a GitHub PAT. `npm install -g` executes the package's install lifecycle scripts, so whatever the registry serves at that moment gets arbitrary code execution on a runner with publishing credentials.

`.github/zizmor.yml` silences zizmor's `adhoc-packages` audit for this file, which suppresses the warning without addressing it.

## Evidence

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:87-89

      - name: Install and enable corepack
        shell: sh
        run: npm install -g corepack --force && corepack enable
```

Twelve lines later, in the same job:

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:103-108

      - name: Semantic Release
        uses: cycjimmy/semantic-release-action@b12c8f6015dc215fe37bc154d4ad456dd3833c90 # v6.0.0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: true
```

The suppression:

```yaml

# .github/zizmor.yml:22-26

  adhoc-packages:
    # corepack must be bootstrapped globally; no lockfile applies
    ignore:
      - publish.yml
      - pr-lint.yml
```

Every other third-party unit in these workflows is pinned to a full commit SHA — `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5…`, `actions/setup-node@8207627…`, `actions/cache@55cc834…`, `cycjimmy/semantic-release-action@b12c8f6…`. `README.md:115-118` states the reasoning explicitly: "Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs rather than `@v4`-style tags: a tag is mutable, and this workflow runs with `contents: write` and an `NPM_TOKEN` in scope." The corepack install is the one dependency in that job exempt from the policy the repo documents.

## Impact

Failure scenario: the corepack package or a maintainer account is compromised and a malicious version is published. The next push to `main` runs `npm install -g corepack --force`, which resolves to that version and runs its install scripts on the runner. The job then proceeds to `semantic-release` with `NPM_TOKEN` and `secrets.PAT` in the environment — the injected code can exfiltrate both, or publish a tampered `@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config` tarball directly.

Because this package is a base config consumed by other `base-configs-*` repositories, a poisoned publish propagates to every downstream project's release pipeline.

The zizmor ignore is what makes this persist: the scanner detects it on every run and the finding is discarded rather than fixed. The stated reason ("no lockfile applies") explains why a lockfile cannot pin it, not why a version cannot.

Node 25 unbundled corepack, so the step cannot simply be deleted while `.nvmrc` pins `v26` — pinning is the available fix, not removal.

## Fix

Pin the version in both workflows that bootstrap it:

```yaml
      - name: Install and enable corepack
        shell: sh
        run: npm install -g <email> --force && corepack enable
```

Use the exact version currently in use, then let Renovate keep it current — add it to `.github/renovate.json` under a `matchManagers: ["npm"]` rule, or track it as a `regexManagers`/`customManagers` entry against the workflow files so bumps arrive as reviewable PRs with the `actions` scope.

Once pinned, narrow the zizmor suppression to state the residual risk, or drop the `adhoc-packages` ignore entirely if pinning satisfies the audit. Apply the same change to `.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:50-52`, which carries no secrets but should not diverge.

## Resolution
Pinned to <email> (verified as the real current version via `npm view corepack version`, not guessed) at both call sites: publish.yml and the new shared test.yml. Comments at each site record why it cannot be dropped (Node 25 unbundled corepack while .nvmrc pins v26) and why it must be pinned (npm install -g runs install scripts next to the publish credentials). Updated the zizmor adhoc-packages ignore to name the residual risk that remains after pinning and to flag re-checking if the pin is ever loosened.

## Problem

The `publish` job requests `contents: write`, `issues: write` and `pull-requests: write` for the automatic `GITHUB_TOKEN`. No step in the job uses that token: `semantic-release` runs with `secrets.PAT` supplied explicitly, and the checkout sets `persist-credentials: false` so no credential is left in the git config either.

The permissions block describes what `@semantic-release/github` needs, but the credential it actually receives is the PAT. The grants are dead — and they are write grants on the job that also holds the npm publish token.

## Evidence

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:66-70

    permissions:
      contents: write # to be able to publish a GitHub release
      issues: write # to be able to comment on released issues
      pull-requests: write # to be able to comment on released pull requests
      id-token: write # to enable use of OIDC for npm provenance
```

The only credentials any step consumes, across all five workflows:

```
$ grep -n 'github.token\|GITHUB_TOKEN\|secrets\.' .github/workflows/*.yml
.github/workflows/publish.yml:106:          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
.github/workflows/publish.yml:107:          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
.github/workflows/sync-labels.yml:40:          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

`publish.yml:106` overrides `GITHUB_TOKEN` with the PAT, so the automatic token never reaches `semantic-release`. The checkout discards it too:

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:73-77

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
```

`id-token: write` is the one scope that is genuinely used — `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: true` on line 108 depends on it.

`CLAUDE.md` confirms nothing else needs `contents: write`: "No changelog file or git commit-back — release notes live on GitHub Releases only." There is no `@semantic-release/git` in the plugin chain (`index.cjs:38-39` ends at npm and github).

## Impact

Failure scenario: the unpinned `npm install -g corepack --force` on line 89 (see the related finding) pulls a compromised package, or `cycjimmy/semantic-release-action` is subverted. Any code executing in this job can read `${{ github.token }}` from the runner environment and, with `contents: write`, force-push to `main` or rewrite tags — capability it does not need and would not have under a correct permissions block.

This widens the blast radius of every other weakness in the same job. Least privilege is the control that keeps a single compromised step from becoming repository write access; here it is granted and then not exercised, which is the worst of both — the risk without the benefit.

Severity is Medium rather than High because exploitation requires a prior compromise inside the job; the grants are not directly reachable by an outside attacker.

## Fix

Reduce the block to what the job actually exercises:

```yaml
    permissions:
      contents: read # to check out the repository
      id-token: write # to enable use of OIDC for npm provenance
```

If the intent is instead to stop using the PAT and let the automatic token do the release, make that switch and keep the write scopes — change line 106 to `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`. That also aligns the workflow with what `README.md:63` tells consumers to use, and removes a long-lived account-scoped credential from the pipeline. The PAT is presumably there to let the release tag trigger downstream workflows; if that is the reason, record it as a comment next to line 106 so the permissions block is not read as the source of truth.

Do not leave the two in their current disagreement — a permissions block that documents a token the job does not use will be trusted by the next reader.

## Resolution
Reduced the publish job to `contents: read` + `id-token: write`, dropping the unused contents/issues/pull-requests write grants. Verified before applying, at the user's request, that this cannot break publishing: cycjimmy/semantic-release-action@b12c8f6 declares no github_token input and no ${{ github.token }} default (fetched action.yml at the pinned SHA); @semantic-release/github/lib/resolve-config.js:27 reads `env.GH_TOKEN || env.GITHUB_TOKEN`, which the workflow sets to secrets.PAT; and semantic-release/lib/get-git-auth-url.js builds a token-bearing remote URL for the tag push rather than using git credentials, which persist-credentials: false discards. id-token: write retained for NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE. Added a comment recording this reasoning so the block is not widened again.
title: Publish job grants three unused write scopes to a GITHUB_TOKEN no step uses

body:
## Problem

`secrets.PAT` and `secrets.NPM_TOKEN` are repository-level secrets injected straight into the `publish` job. There is no `environment:` key, so nothing gates which workflow runs may read them — no required reviewers, no branch restriction, no deployment-protection rule.

zizmor reports this at High confidence on both lines. It is the only unignored finding it raises against this repository.

## Evidence

```
$ zizmor --no-online-audits --persona=auditor .github/workflows/
warning[secrets-outside-env]: secrets referenced without a dedicated environment
   --> .github/workflows/publish.yml:106:29
    |
 60 |   publish:
    |   ------- this job
...
106 |           GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT }}
    |                             ^^^^^^^^^^^ secret is accessed outside of a dedicated environment
    |
    = note: audit confidence → High

warning[secrets-outside-env]: secrets referenced without a dedicated environment
   --> .github/workflows/publish.yml:107:26
    |
107 |           NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    |                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ secret is accessed outside of a dedicated environment

6 findings (4 ignored): 0 informational, 0 low, 2 medium, 0 high
```

The job declares no environment:

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:60-71

  publish:
    name: Publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs:
      - Linter
      - test
    permissions:
      contents: write
      ...
```

The other four zizmor findings are suppressed deliberately and with stated reasons in `.github/zizmor.yml`; these two are not, so they surface on every scan and on every MegaLinter run (`ACTION_ZIZMOR` is in the `ENABLE_LINTERS` allowlist at `.mega-linter.yml:31`).

## Impact

Failure scenario: any workflow change that adds a new trigger to `publish.yml` — a `workflow_dispatch` for manual reruns, a `workflow_call` so another repo can invoke it — immediately exposes both credentials to whoever can fire that trigger. Repository secrets carry no independent guard; the `on: push: branches: [main]` restriction at lines 4-7 is the *only* thing limiting access, and it lives in the same file a contributor might edit.

An Environment moves that control out of the workflow file and under branch/reviewer protection, so a workflow edit alone cannot widen access to the npm publish token.

The exposure is compounded here because `secrets.PAT` is an account-scoped personal access token rather than the job-scoped automatic token: its blast radius extends past this repository.

Left as-is, the two warnings also become permanent noise in the linter output, which trains readers to ignore zizmor results.

## Fix

Create a repository Environment (for example `npm-publish`), move `PAT` and `NPM_TOKEN` into it as environment secrets, delete the repository-level copies, and reference it from the job:

```yaml
  publish:
    name: Publish
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: npm-publish
    needs:
      - Linter
      - test
```

In the Environment settings, restrict deployment branches to `main`. Add required reviewers if manual approval before a publish is wanted; the branch restriction alone already closes the trigger-widening path above.

If a gate is explicitly not wanted, suppress it the way the other four are — add `secrets-outside-env` to `.github/zizmor.yml` with a comment stating why the risk is accepted. Do not leave it reported-and-ignored; that is the state that erodes the value of the scanner.

## Resolution
Added `environment: npm-publish` to the publish job. zizmor now reports zero findings where it previously reported two mediums. NOTE: the workflow half is done but the protection is not active until the repository settings change — PAT and NPM_TOKEN must be moved from repository secrets to that environment and its deployment branches restricted to main. Until then they still resolve as repository secrets, so publishing is unaffected but no gate is enforced. Comment in the workflow states this.
title: Publish secrets are reachable without a GitHub Environment gate (zizmor secrets-outside-env)

body:
## Problem

The `publish` job's dependency setup differs from every other install in the repository in two ways, both of which weaken the guarantee that what gets published is what got tested:

1. It runs bare `yarn install`, while the `test` job in the same file and the one in `pr-lint.yml` both run `yarn install --immutable`. The highest-privilege job has the least strict install.
2. It restores `node_modules` from a cache keyed on `hashFiles('**/yarn.lock')` alone — no runner OS, no Node version. On a cache hit the install step is skipped entirely, so the tree is whatever was archived on some earlier run.

## Evidence

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:91-101

      - name: Cache Node Modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        id: cache
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: node-modules-${{ hashFiles('**/yarn.lock') }}

      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: yarn install
```

The two jobs that gate it, by contrast:

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:52-54 (test job)

      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: yarn install --immutable
```

```yaml

# .github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:54-56

      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: yarn install --immutable
```

The node version is taken from a file the cache key does not cover:

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:79-83

      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          always-auth: true
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
```

`.nvmrc` currently reads `v26`.

## Impact

Failure scenario for the cache key: a commit bumps `.nvmrc` from `v26` to `v27` without touching `yarn.lock` — a routine change, and one this repo makes (`1dbe3c1 chore(deps): update node, deps and workflows`). The key is unchanged, so the publish job restores a `node_modules` resolved and built under Node 26, skips the install, and runs `semantic-release` against it on Node 27. The `test` job has no cache and installs fresh, so it validates a different tree than the one that publishes. The mismatch is invisible: both jobs go green.

Failure scenario for the mutable install: on a cache miss, `yarn install` may rewrite `yarn.lock` in the publish workspace rather than failing. `semantic-release` then publishes from a resolution the lockfile never recorded and no reviewer saw. `--immutable` turns that into a hard failure, which is the correct outcome in a job that pushes to npm.

Neither is currently exploitable by an outsider, and the `needs: [Linter, test]` gate catches lockfile drift before publish — which is why this is Medium, not High. What it costs is the property the pipeline is supposed to have: the artifact that ships is built from the tree that passed.

## Fix

Make the publish install match the tested one and key the cache on everything that changes the tree:

```yaml
      - name: Cache Node Modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        id: cache
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: node-modules-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('.nvmrc', 'yarn.lock') }}

      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: yarn install --immutable
```

Narrowing `**/yarn.lock` to `yarn.lock` is deliberate: the glob would also match a lockfile inside any nested directory, which is not what the key is meant to track.

Simpler alternative worth considering: delete the cache step. This repository's install is small enough that the cache saves little, and removing it makes the publish job identical to the test job — no key to keep correct, no skip-install branch, and the mutable/immutable divergence cannot reappear.

## Resolution
Publish job now runs `yarn install --immutable`, matching the test job that gates it. Cache key changed from `node-modules-${{ hashFiles('**/yarn.lock') }}` to `node-modules-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('.nvmrc', 'yarn.lock') }}` — adds the runner OS and .nvmrc so a Node bump without a lockfile change no longer hits a stale cache, and narrows the glob so a nested lockfile cannot influence the key. Comments record both reasons.
title: Publish job installs mutably from a cache keyed only on yarn.lock, so it can ship a tree the test job never ran

body:
## Problem

`index.d.ts` is published and advertised as the package's type surface via both `"types"` and the first key of the `exports` map. Nothing in the repository ever compiles it.

There is no `tsconfig.json`, no `typecheck` script, and `typescript` is not declared in `package.json` at all — it resolves only as a transitive of `@ivuorinen/eslint-config`. ESLint lints seven files and `index.d.ts` is not among them. The only test touching it asserts that the file exists on disk.

## Evidence

The declaration depends on a type imported from a package whose major version this repo tracks:

```ts
// index.d.ts:1-5
import type { GlobalConfig } from "semantic-release";

declare const config: GlobalConfig;

export default config;
```

No typechecking exists:

```
$ grep -n 'typescript' package.json
typescript NOT in package.json

$ node -e "console.log(require('typescript/package.json').version)"
7.0.2                      # transitive via @ivuorinen/eslint-config, not declared

$ ls tsconfig.json
no tsconfig

$ node -e "console.log(Object.keys(require('./package.json').scripts).join(','))"
lint,postinstall,test
```

ESLint does not cover it:

```
$ npx eslint . --format=json
files linted: 7
eslint.config.mjs, index.cjs, scripts/postinstall.cjs,
test/config-shape.test.mjs, test/postinstall.test.mjs,
test/release-rules.test.mjs, wrapper.mjs
```

The only assertion about the file checks existence, not validity:

```js
// test/config-shape.test.mjs:85-91
test("every entry point declared in package.json exists on disk", () => {
  const declared = [pkg.main, pkg.module, pkg.types, ...Object.values(pkg.exports)];
  for (const entry of declared) {
    const resolved = fileURLToPath(new URL(`../${entry.replace(/^\.\//u, "")}`, import.meta.url));
    assert.ok(fs.existsSync(resolved), `${entry} is declared in package.json but missing`);
  }
});
```

And it is in the published tarball:

```
$ npm pack --dry-run
LICENSE.md  README.md  index.cjs  index.d.ts  package.json
scripts/postinstall.cjs  wrapper.mjs
```

## Impact

Failure scenario: `semantic-release` releases v26 and renames or removes the exported `GlobalConfig` type — a plausible change, since `CLAUDE.md` documents `chore(deps)!` bumps of `semantic-release` as routine, and `8936758 chore(deps)!: update semantic-release (24.2.3 - 25.0.0)` is already in history. `index.d.ts:1` then fails to resolve its import.

Nothing catches it. `yarn test` passes — all 42 tests are runtime assertions about the CJS object, and the one test that names `index.d.ts` only stats it. ESLint skips it. MegaLinter's `ENABLE_LINTERS` allowlist (`.mega-linter.yml:29-34`) contains no TypeScript entry. CodeQL analyses `javascript`, not declaration validity.

The broken declaration ships. Every TypeScript consumer importing the config gets a compile error inside `node_modules`, attributable to this package, discovered only after publication.

The undeclared `typescript` dependency is the second half of the problem: even a maintainer who runs `tsc` locally is exercising a version that arrived by accident through a lint config, and would vanish if that config dropped it.

## Fix

Declare the toolchain and wire the check into the existing verification path.

Add to `devDependencies`:

```json
"typescript": "^7.0.2"
```

Add `tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "skipLibCheck": false,
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "module": "preserve",
    "target": "es2022"
  },
  "include": ["index.d.ts"]
}
```

Add the script and make it part of `test`, so CI picks it up with no workflow change (both `publish.yml` and `pr-lint.yml` already run `yarn test`):

```json
"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
"test": "yarn typecheck && node --test \"test/**/*.test.mjs\""
```

For a stronger assertion than "it compiles", add a fixture that pins the contract the package promises:

```ts
// test/types.test-d.ts — included in tsconfig
import config from "../index.cjs";
const branches: readonly unknown[] | unknown = config.branches;
const plugins: unknown = config.plugins;
```

Then update `CLAUDE.md`'s Verification section, which currently names only `yarn test` and the config-load one-liner, to state that `yarn test` now also typechecks the published declarations.

## Resolution
Declared typescript@^7.0.2 and @types/node as devDependencies, added tsconfig.json scoped to index.d.ts, added a `typecheck` script, and wired it into `test` so both CI workflows pick it up without a workflow change. skipLibCheck is deliberately false — turning it on would skip index.d.ts itself, since that is a declaration file, making the check a no-op; noImplicitAny is off because skipLibCheck:false pulls in semantic-release's declarations, which import the untyped signale package. Both decisions are documented in the tsconfig root "//" key (TypeScript rejects unknown keys inside compilerOptions and the pretty-format-json hook rejects JSONC comments). Verified with a negative control: aliasing the import to a nonexistent type produced TS2614, confirming the check is not vacuous. yarn test 43/43 with typecheck running first.
title: Shipped type declarations are never typechecked — no tsconfig, no typecheck script, typescript undeclared

body:
## Problem

`index.d.ts` types the exported object as `GlobalConfig`. In semantic-release's own declarations `GlobalConfig` means "options after normalization and defaults have been applied" — the resolved runtime configuration, not the input a shareable config provides.

This package exports the opposite thing: a partial configuration consumed via `extends`, merged with the consumer's own settings, and normalized afterwards by semantic-release. `Options` is the type for that.

It compiles because `GlobalConfig extends Options` and every member is optional, so the error is semantic rather than structural — the declaration promises consumers a normalized config they are not receiving.

## Evidence

```ts
// index.d.ts:1-5
import type { GlobalConfig } from "semantic-release";

declare const config: GlobalConfig;

export default config;
```

semantic-release states what the type means directly above its definition:

```ts
// node_modules/semantic-release/index.d.ts:442-447
  /**
   * semantic-release options, after normalization and defaults have been
   * applied.
   */
  export interface GlobalConfig extends Options {
```

The exported object is plainly pre-normalization — four keys, no defaults resolved:

```js
// index.cjs:3-5
module.exports = {
  branches: ["main"],
  plugins: [
```

and it is consumed by reference, not by value:

```json
// .releaserc.json
{ "extends": ["./index.cjs"] }
```

`README.md:51-57` documents the same contract for consumers:

```json
{
  "extends": ["@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config"]
}
```

## Impact

Failure scenario: a consumer writes TypeScript that builds on the config — merging it, or reading a field to decide something:

```ts
import base from "@ivuorinen/semantic-release-config";
const tagFormat: string | undefined = base.tagFormat;
```

`GlobalConfig` tells them `tagFormat` is a property of a *normalized* config, so the natural reading is that defaults are present and the value is populated. It is `undefined` — `index.cjs` never sets it, and normalization has not run. The type does not prevent the mistake; it suggests it.

The same applies to `repositoryUrl`, `tagFormat`, `dryRun`, `ci` and every other key semantic-release fills in during normalization: the declaration implies they are resolved when none of them are.

Low severity: all members are optional in both types, so no consumer build breaks and no runtime behaviour changes. It is a wrong claim in the published type surface rather than a defect, and the fix is one word.

## Fix

Use the input type:

```ts
import type { Options } from "semantic-release";

/**
 * The shared semantic-release configuration, consumed via `extends`.
 *
 * Typed as `Options` rather than `GlobalConfig`: this is pre-normalization
 * input that semantic-release merges with the consumer's own settings, so the
 * defaults `GlobalConfig` implies are not present on this object.
 */
declare const config: Options;

export default config;
```

Verify the change compiles by adding the typecheck wiring tracked in the separate finding on this file — without it, this edit is as unverified as the current declaration.

## Resolution
index.d.ts now imports and declares `Options` instead of `GlobalConfig`, with a docstring explaining that GlobalConfig is semantic-release's post-normalization type and that none of the defaults it implies (tagFormat, repositoryUrl, ci) are present on a shareable config. Verified by the typecheck wired up in audit-e1de321b.
title: Config is typed as GlobalConfig, semantic-release's post-normalization type, not Options

body:
## Problem

Both contributor-facing documents describe a repository state that no longer exists. They predate `index.d.ts`, the two new test files, and the `lint` script, and `CLAUDE.md`'s Verification section names a test glob that does not match the one `package.json` runs.

These are the two files a new contributor and a coding agent read first to learn what the repo contains and how to verify a change.

## Evidence

`CLAUDE.md:5-11` lists one test file; three exist, and `index.d.ts` is absent from the list entirely:

```markdown
## Key Files

- `index.cjs` — the shared config (commit-analyzer rules, release-notes types, plugin chain)
- `wrapper.mjs` — ESM re-export of `index.cjs`
- `scripts/postinstall.cjs` — auto-creates `.releaserc.json` in consuming projects
- `.releaserc.json` — this repo's own release config, extends `./index.cjs`
- `test/release-rules.test.mjs` — asserts the release each commit pattern produces
```

Actual test files:

```
test/config-shape.test.mjs
test/postinstall.test.mjs
test/release-rules.test.mjs
```

`CLAUDE.md:19` states the wrong glob:

```markdown
Runs `node --test` over `test/*.test.mjs`, feeding real commit messages through
```

versus `package.json`:

```json
"test": "node --test \"test/**/*.test.mjs\""
```

`CLAUDE.md:45-51` (Code Quality) lists only the pre-commit hooks and omits the `lint` script that now exists:

```json
"lint": "eslint .",
```

`CONTRIBUTING.md:50-53` repeats the same incomplete key-file list:

```markdown
2. Make your changes. The key files are:
   - `index.cjs` — the shared semantic-release configuration
   - `wrapper.mjs` — ESM wrapper that re-exports `index.cjs`
   - `scripts/postinstall.cjs` — auto-creates `.releaserc.json` in consuming projects
```

and `CONTRIBUTING.md:55-63` describes `yarn test` as if it only exercised commit-analyzer:

```markdown
   These feed real commit messages through `@semantic-release/commit-analyzer`
   and assert the exact release each one cuts. Any change to `index.cjs` needs
   them to pass.
```

That is true of 33 of the 42 tests; the other 9 assert config shape, the exports map, and postinstall behaviour.

`CONTRIBUTING.md:71-85` (Code Quality) likewise omits `yarn lint`.

## Impact

Failure scenario: a contributor changes `index.cjs`, consults `CLAUDE.md`, sees `index.d.ts` mentioned nowhere, and does not update the declaration to match. Nothing catches it — the declaration is not typechecked either (tracked separately) — and the type surface silently drifts from the runtime config.

The wrong glob is the more actively misleading line: a contributor who adds `test/nested/foo.test.mjs` and reads "`node --test` over `test/*.test.mjs`" will conclude it is not picked up, when in fact `test/**/*.test.mjs` does run it. A reader who trusts the doc over the manifest reaches the wrong conclusion about their own test.

Omitting `yarn lint` means the linter is discoverable only by reading `package.json`, so contributors hit ESLint failures in CI rather than locally — the exact cost the Code Quality sections exist to prevent.

Low severity: nothing breaks at runtime, and the drift is cheap to correct. It is filed because `CLAUDE.md` is the instruction file an agent treats as authoritative, where a stale list is followed rather than questioned.

## Fix

In `CLAUDE.md`, extend the key-file list and correct the glob:

```markdown
## Key Files

- `index.cjs` — the shared config (commit-analyzer rules, release-notes types, plugin chain)
- `wrapper.mjs` — ESM re-export of `index.cjs`
- `index.d.ts` — published type declarations for the exported config
- `scripts/postinstall.cjs` — auto-creates `.releaserc.json` in consuming projects
- `.releaserc.json` — this repo's own release config, extends `./index.cjs`
- `test/release-rules.test.mjs` — asserts the release each commit pattern produces
- `test/config-shape.test.mjs` — asserts the plugin chain, preset, and exports map
- `test/postinstall.test.mjs` — asserts the postinstall scaffold behaviour
```

Change line 19 from `test/*.test.mjs` to `test/**/*.test.mjs`, and add `yarn lint` to the Code Quality section alongside `pre-commit run --all-files`.

Apply the same two additions to `CONTRIBUTING.md`: add `index.d.ts` to the key-file list at lines 50-53, and add a `yarn lint` step to the Code Quality section at lines 71-85. Reword lines 61-63 so the test description covers all three files rather than only the commit-analyzer cases.

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md: key-file list now includes index.d.ts, tsconfig.json and all three test files; the glob is corrected from test/*.test.mjs to test/**/*.test.mjs; the Verification section describes the typecheck step and lists yarn lint and yarn typecheck; Code Quality notes the shared CI test workflow. CONTRIBUTING.md: index.d.ts added to the key files with a note to update it alongside index.cjs, the test description now covers all three suites plus the typecheck, and Code Quality states explicitly that ESLint is not a pre-commit hook and must be run manually.
title: CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md key-file lists and verification steps are stale
