## Problem

`README.md` ships a complete, copy-pasteable release workflow as the recommended integration. It pins `node-version: 20`. Node 20 left Maintenance LTS in April 2026 and receives no further security patches.

The example is otherwise carefully maintained — every action is pinned to a full commit SHA, `permissions: {}` is set at workflow level, `persist-credentials: false` and `fetch-depth: 0` are both present. The Node pin is the one line that has not kept pace.

## Evidence

```yaml

# README.md:96-102

      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          always-auth: true
          node-version: 20
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
```

The same step in this repository's own workflow reads the version from a file instead, and that file is four majors ahead:

```yaml

# .github/workflows/publish.yml:79-83

      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          always-auth: true
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
```

```
$ cat .nvmrc
v26
```

`package.json` declares `"engines": { "node": ">=20" }`, so 20 satisfies the floor — the pin is not invalid, it is merely the oldest value the floor permits, presented as the recommendation.

`CONTRIBUTING.md:16` carries the same floor as a prerequisite: "[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) >= 20".

## Impact

Failure scenario: a consumer copies the README workflow verbatim — which is what a copy-pasteable block invites — and their release pipeline runs on an unpatched Node runtime. That job holds `NPM_TOKEN` and `contents: write`, the highest-privilege job in their repository, so it is the worst place to run an unsupported runtime.

A second, quieter cost: the example diverges from what this repository actually tests. `semantic-release ^25.0.5` is exercised here on Node 26 only. A consumer on Node 20 is running an untested combination, and any incompatibility surfaces as a release failure they will attribute to this config.

Low severity because the guidance is copied, not executed by this repository, and `>=20` remains a truthful floor. It is filed because the README's own closing paragraph (lines 115-118) explains the reasoning behind the SHA pinning — the file sets an explicit standard of security-conscious example code, and this line does not meet it.

## Fix

Point the example at a supported release and keep it from ageing again:

```yaml
      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          always-auth: true
          node-version: 24
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
```

Use the current Active LTS. Prefer `node-version-file: ".nvmrc"` if the surrounding prose tells consumers to keep an `.nvmrc` — that is what this repo does for itself and it removes the number from the README entirely, so the example cannot go stale.

Separately, decide whether `"engines": { "node": ">=20" }` still reflects the supported range. If Node 20 is no longer supported, raise the floor and say so in a `feat!:` commit so consumers get the major bump the release rules are designed to deliver. If 20 is still supported, leave the floor and add one line under the example noting that the pin shows the recommended version, not the minimum.

## Resolution
README workflow example now pins node-version: 24 (current Active LTS) instead of 20. Added a paragraph after the example stating that the pin shows the recommended version rather than the >=20 floor, that Node 20 is end-of-life and should not run a release job, and pointing at node-version-file: ".nvmrc" as the alternative. The engines floor itself was left at >=20 — narrowing it is a breaking change for consumers and belongs in a deliberate feat! commit, not an audit fix.
title: The documented consumer workflow pins Node 20, which is end-of-life

body:
## Problem

`pr-lint.yml` and `publish.yml` each define a `test` job. The two are byte-identical across all six steps — same checkout SHA, same setup-node SHA, same corepack bootstrap, same `yarn install --immutable`, same `yarn test`, same permissions, same timeout.

One is the pre-merge gate, the other the pre-publish gate. They must stay in agreement, and nothing enforces that they do.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/pr-lint.yml:32-60`:

```yaml
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read # to check out the repository

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"

      - name: Install and enable corepack
        shell: sh
        run: npm install -g corepack --force && corepack enable

      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: yarn install --immutable

      - name: Run Tests
        shell: bash
        run: yarn test
```

`.github/workflows/publish.yml:30-58` is the same 29 lines. The `Linter` job is duplicated too, at `pr-lint.yml:18-30` and `publish.yml:16-28`.

Both were added in the same change — `resolved.jsonl` records the fix for `audit-c9272141`: "Added a test job to publish.yml (publish now needs: [Linter, test]) and to pr-lint.yml so PRs fail before merge."

## Impact

Failure scenario: the pinned `npm install -g corepack` gets a version (the fix for a separate finding on this file), or `.nvmrc` handling changes, or a `yarn typecheck` step is added to the test job — and the edit lands in one file. The two gates now test differently. The pre-merge gate passes, the pre-publish gate fails, and the failure appears on `main` after merge rather than on the PR. Or the reverse, which is worse: the pre-publish gate is the weaker of the two and publishes something the PR gate would have caught.

There is no mechanism that detects the divergence. `actionlint` validates each file in isolation and reports nothing; both currently pass clean.

Low severity: the duplication is correct today, both workflows are short, and the consequence is a delayed signal rather than a broken release. Filed because every fix proposed against `publish.yml` in this audit has a twin in `pr-lint.yml` that must be applied by hand — which is precisely how the two drift apart.

## Fix

Extract the shared job into a reusable workflow and call it from both.

`.github/workflows/test.yml`:

```yaml
---
name: Test

on:
  workflow_call:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read # to check out the repository

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js Environment
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"

      - name: Install and enable corepack
        shell: sh
        run: npm install -g <email> --force && corepack enable

      - name: Install Dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: yarn install --immutable

      - name: Run Tests
        shell: bash
        run: yarn test
```

Then in both callers:

```yaml
  test:
    name: Test
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test.yml
```

`publish.yml`'s `needs: [Linter, test]` continues to work unchanged — a called workflow's job satisfies `needs` under the calling job's id.

The `Linter` job is a single `uses:` step in both files, so the same treatment is optional there; the cost of duplicating one line is lower than the indirection.

If a reusable workflow is judged heavier than the problem, the acceptable alternative is a comment at the top of each `test` job naming its twin, so the next editor knows to change both. Do not leave them silently paired.

## Resolution
Extracted the duplicated job into .github/workflows/test.yml as a workflow_call reusable workflow; pr-lint.yml and publish.yml both now call it with a four-line `uses: ./.github/workflows/test.yml` job. publish.yml's `needs: [Linter, test]` continues to resolve against the calling job id. The Linter job stays duplicated as the finding allowed — it is a single `uses:` line and the indirection would cost more than it saves. actionlint clean on all six workflows.
title: The test job is duplicated verbatim between pr-lint.yml and publish.yml
